visual_requirements.description: Falcon-headed male Ra-Harahkhte variant with Egyptian double crown and sun disk; opaque clothing.
Sun domain represented by strong actual sunlight and sharp shadows, no invented powers.

depicted_variant: Documented Ra-Harahkhte fusion: falcon-headed Horus with double crown and sun disk.
aura: Double crown with sun disk(c06), defender of order(c11) rising from throne(c22).
artistic_choices: Opaque gold-trimmed linen ceremonial attire editorial.
Sunlight only; no extra wings on human body, invented giant scale or weapon.
Crown and sun disk enlarged within frame via perspective, not claim of giant physical size.

prompts.A:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mythics illustration of Horus as documented Ra-Harahkhte, falcon-headed sun god and royal defender.
ANATOMY: ONE falcon head with two eyes hooked beak and feathered cheeks, human male body with exactly two arms two legs, fully opaque dark linen tunic and ankle-length wrap, Egyptian DOUBLE CROWN combining white tall crown and red lower crown, large ROUND gold sun disk on crown [horus-c06]. NO wings added to human body.
POWER: sun domain embodied through real low sun lighting crown and casting long sharp shadows, NO invented magic [horus-c06].
SCALE & CAMERA: extreme low CLOSE angle, falcon head doublecrown/disk dominate, no giant size.
LIGHT: single dying warm sun through doorway, dust, deep black-gold shadows.
SURFACE: real falcon feathers, weathered metal, rough opaque woven cloth, stone.
SETTING: Egyptian royal throne and plain unlettered palace stone [horus-c22,c23].
MOOD: imposing protective royal authority, awe-inspiring and alert, never decorative neutral statue.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: no hieroglyphs/pseudo-letters or text anywhere on crown/throne/walls/clothes, no logos/borders/watermarks, no extra anatomy, no film/game/anime designs, no nudity/gore, no aura/neon/ribbons.
MOMENT: Horus surges up from throne, one hand grips stone armrest with visible weight, other adjusts his doublecrown as he turns falcon face down toward viewer. Tight frontal three-quarter view.
